name: Delaiah
overview: Delaiah was a male Levite who served as the twenty-third chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in Israel. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, a significant priestly lineage within the tribe of Levi. His role highlights the organized structure of priestly service in ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Delaiah means 'YHWH draws up [like water in a bucket],' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's active involvement. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:18, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to divine provision.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Delaiah as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to a prominent priestly family within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this lineage, no additional family relationships are documented for him.
scriptureSignificance: Delaiah's significance lies in his appointment as one of the twenty-four priestly divisions, specifically the twenty-third course, which organized the Levitical priesthood for service in the temple. His inclusion in the line of Eleazar underscores the continuity of priestly duties passed down through generations. This structured priestly system was vital for maintaining the worship and sacrificial practices commanded by God.
